results.output_text:
Autoregressive local inference is slow because the model must generate one token at a time, waiting for the previous one to finish before starting the next. This creates a long "idle" period where the GPU sits doing nothing while waiting for the next token to be computed.

CUDA graphs solve this by pre-planning the entire sequence of operations for a batch of tokens before execution begins. Instead of the GPU deciding what to do at every single step, the graph is a fixed roadmap that tells the hardware exactly which calculations to perform and in what order, eliminating the decision-making overhead.
